category_title: Grade 1 students who struggle with writing and self-regulation but benefit from oral discourse
minimal_context: Joshua is comparing area R and area M on a worksheet using smaller units of area.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's compare area R and area M on the worksheet using these smaller units of area.

STUDENT: They are not equal, they are not the same.

TUTOR: Can you show me how you figured that out?

STUDENT: (Inspects the figures on the worksheet without touching the units) I just know by looking at them.

TUTOR: I want you to use the area pieces.

STUDENT: No, I want to make the shape of R. Give me the tracing paper so I can copy the figure instead.

options.A: Have the student present to the class and 'think out loud' at the document camera, responding to prompts and peer comments.
options.B: Allow the student to work at his own pace on the worksheet and take a break from the activity whenever he wants.
options.C: Leave the student free to choose any format and materials he likes, such as the tracing paper, to compare the areas.
options.D: Provide a clear beginning and end for the task of comparing the areas on the worksheet during this specific class session.
